instruction:
You have been given a Verilog module named "tb" that instantiates a "cpci_clock_checker" module. The "cpci_clock_checker" module checks the frequency of two clocks, p_clk and n_clk, and generates an error signal if the frequency of either clock is out of range. The input signals to the "cpci_clock_checker" module are as follows:

- error: a 1-bit output signal that indicates whether an error has been detected.
- clk_chk_p_max: a 32-bit input signal that specifies the maximum frequency of the p_clk signal.
- clk_chk_n_exp: a 32-bit input signal that specifies the expected frequency of the n_clk signal.
- reset: a 1-bit input signal that resets the "cpci_clock_checker" module.
- shift_amount: a 4-bit input signal that specifies the amount by which the "cpci_clock_checker" module should shift the frequency of the n_clk signal before comparing it with the expected frequency.
- p_clk: a 1-bit input signal that represents the positive edge of the p_clk clock.
- n_clk: a 1-bit input signal that represents the negative edge of the n_clk clock.

The "tb" module drives the p_clk and n_clk signals and checks the error output signal of the "cpci_clock_checker" module. The "tb" module first drives a reset signal to the "cpci_clock_checker" module and waits for it to assert its "done" signal. When the "cpci_clock_checker" module is done, the "tb" module checks the error signal and displays the error message if an error has been detected. The "tb" module then stops the n_clk signal and waits for the "cpci_clock_checker" module to assert its "done" signal again. When the "cpci_clock_checker" module is done, the "tb" module checks the error signal again and displays the error message if an error has been detected.

Your task is to implement the "cpci_clock_checker" module that checks the frequency of the p_clk and n_clk signals and generates an error signal if the frequency of either clock is out of range.
